title: [dropcounter] Failed to clear dropcounter for non-root user
author: bingwang-ms
body:

You do NOT have to include this information if this is a FEATURE REQUEST
-->

**Description**

<!--
Briefly describe the problem you are having in a few paragraphs.
-->
Non-root user is not able to clear dropcounter if the path ```/tmp/dropstat/``` was created by root.
**Steps to reproduce the issue:**
1. Run ```sudo show dropcounters counts```. The command will create path ```/tmp/dropstat/```, which is owned by ```root```.
```
admin@str-dx010-acs-4:/tmp$ ls -al
drwxr-xr-x 2 root  root   4096 Oct 13 05:37 dropstat
```
2. Run ```show dropcounters counts``` as a non-root user, and we can see there is some recorded drops.
```
admin@str-dx010-acs-4:/tmp$ show dropcounters counts 
  IFACE    STATE    RX_ERR    RX_DROPS    TX_ERR    TX_DROPS    TEST
-----------  -------  --------  ----------  --------  ----------  ------
  Ethernet0        X         0           0         0           0       0
  Ethernet4        U         0           0         0           0       0
  Ethernet8        U         0        1000         0           0       0
 Ethernet12        U         0           0         0           0       0
 Ethernet16        U         0           0         0           0       0
```
3. Run ```sonic-clear dropcounters ```, and an error is reported, and dropcounter is not cleared
```
admin@str-dx010-acs-4:/tmp$ sonic-clear dropcounters 
[Errno 13] Permission denied: '/tmp/dropstat/port-stats-1000'
admin@str-dx010-acs-4:/tmp$ show dropcounters counts 
      IFACE    STATE    RX_ERR    RX_DROPS    TX_ERR    TX_DROPS    TEST
-----------  -------  --------  ----------  --------  ----------  ------
  Ethernet0        X         0           0         0           0       0
  Ethernet4        U         0           0         0           0       0
  Ethernet8        U         0        1000         0           0       0
 Ethernet12        U         0           0         0           0       0
 Ethernet16        U         0           0         0           0       0
```
The issue is caused by ```/usr/local/bin/dropstat```, which creates the path ```/tmp/dropstat/``` if not exists, and attempts to create dump files in this path when dropcounter is to be cleared. However, there is no write permission for other users except for the path owner.  
This issue exists in both 201911 and master branch.
Besides, the ```configurable dropcounter``` was found not work as expected on master branch. I'm not sure if it's caused by the same reason.

 
**Describe the results you received:**
Dropcounter is not cleared as expected.

**Describe the results you expected:**
Dropcounter is cleared as expected.

**Additional information you deem important (e.g. issue happens only occasionally):**

    **Output of `show version`:**


comments.author: daall
comments.body: I tried to model this after `portstat` but I missed one key detail - each user has a tmp *directory* to store the checkpoints. I will implement this for drop counters as well.

linkedPullRequests.title: [dropcounters] Fix clear for non-root users
linkedPullRequests.author: daall
linkedPullRequests.body:
Signed-off-by: Danny Allen <daall@microsoft.com>

<!--
Please make sure you've read and understood our contributing guidelines:

If this is a bug fix, make sure your description includes "closes #xxxx",

If you are adding/modifying/removing any command or utility script, please also
make sure to add/modify/remove any unit tests from the tests
directory as appropriate.

If you are modifying or removing an existing 'show', 'config' or 'sonic-clear'
subcommand, or you are adding a new subcommand, please make sure you also
update the Command Line Reference Guide (doc/Command-Reference.md) to reflect
your changes.

Please provide the following information:
-->

**- What I did**
Fixes https://github.com/Azure/sonic-buildimage/issues/5602

**- How I did it**
I followed the same pattern from `portstat` and gave each user their own `dropstat` directory instead of indexing the files by uid.

**- How to verify it**
Validated that non-root user can clear after a `sudo sonic-clear dropcounters`. Also verified that each uid has their own `/tmp` directory. Also updated the unit tests.
